_source: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing fetched 2026-09-06; USD per million tokens; cache_write is the 5-minute rate. meter_weight is meter percent per list dollar relative to Sonnet 5; Fable's 1.0 is measured: the 2026-09-06 5-tick Fable probe cost $1.08 of list value per 1% against $0.98 for Sonnet on the same cache-write-heavy payload (ratio 0.91, within probe error). class_weight is meter percent per list dollar for each token class relative to cache_write, the class the Sonnet probe is made of. class_weight.output is maintained by the publisher (tracker/weight.py): the weekly Sunday Fable output run (bin/output-probe.sh, payload output) supplies a row, and the next daily publish solves the weight at which that row and the latest Fable prose row read the same meter dollars per 1%, writes it to every model here, and records the pair under _output_weight; a value more than 30% from the current one is refused, recorded with applied false, and alerts Jonathan instead. The 1.8 hand-entered on 2026-09-06 was the crude ratio of the two rows' list values; the first automatic recompute from the same pair gave 1.95 because the output row's own cache traffic (12% of its list value) sits on the unweighted side. input and cache_read are unmeasured and assumed 1.0; the same class weights are assumed for every model. Opus 5's 1.0 is measured too: a paired run on the Jono Work account on 2026-09-08, same 5-hour window, cost $0.918 of list value per 1% for Opus (ticks 7 to 10) against $0.963 for Sonnet (ticks 2 to 5), ratio 0.954, within probe error, so Opus keeps meter_weight 1.0. The first Opus row (2026-09-07 on Dave, $0.682 per 1%, early tick) is flagged outlier by hand under the rotation's own decide rule: the later same-model reading agreed with the all-model median, not with it.
